# An accumulator of two limbs: add a product of the guarded factors

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `acc_mul_entry_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A step of an accumulator: the running sum $t \approx s + x y$, and the sum of the magnitudes $b$ rounded to a number of `T`:

$$t \approx s + x y, \qquad b = \mathrm{RN}(a + \lvert x_0\rvert \lvert y_0\rvert).$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $s = s_0 + s_1$, $x = x_0 + x_1$, $y = y_0 + y_1$, $t = t_0 + t_1$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `A.add_product(x, y)` | `Accumulator<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>`, `Expansion<T, 2>` | `void` | one more term; the bound of the whole history is `A.error_bound()` ([Accumulator](accumulator.md)); not `constexpr`; each limb of each factor guarded (rule R3 on the factors of a fused operation) |
| `A.add_product(a, b)` | `Accumulator<T, 2>`, `T`, `T` | `void` | each value of `T` converted to `Expansion<T, 2>` first, exactly (`make_2`) |

`T` is `float` or `double`; `A` and `B` are accumulators, `kairn::Accumulator<T, k>`, header `kairn/accumulator.hpp`, which `kairn/kairn.hpp` includes. They take no marker: an operation of an accumulator compiles only while its kernels are proved ([The accumulator](accumulator.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $s$ is normalized: $s_0 = \mathrm{RN}(s_0 + s_1)$.
- $x$ is normalized: $x_0 = \mathrm{RN}(x_0 + x_1)$.
- $y$ is normalized: $y_0 = \mathrm{RN}(y_0 + y_1)$.
- $a \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $t$ is normalized: $t_0 = \mathrm{RN}(t_0 + t_1)$.
- $\lvert t - (s + x y)\rvert \le \left(\frac{3(1 + 4u u)}{1 - 4u} + 4\right) u^2\,(\lvert s\rvert + \lvert x y\rvert) + 2\,\eta$.
- $b = \mathrm{RN}(a + \lvert x_0\rvert \lvert y_0\rvert)$: the number of the format nearest to $a + \lvert x_0\rvert \lvert y_0\rvert$, ties to even.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u^2$ | $\approx 8.6282 \times 10^{-32}$ | $\approx 2.4869 \times 10^{-14}$ |
| absolute term $t\,\eta$ | $2^{-1073} \approx 9.8813 \times 10^{-324}$ | $2^{-148} \approx 2.8026 \times 10^{-45}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1.c000000000002p-104`, `0x1p-1073` | `0x1.c00004p-46f`, `0x1p-148f` |

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 4 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `acc_mul_entry_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/AccKernels.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/AccKernels.v), against `acc_mul_entry_2_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions acc_mul_entry_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition acc_mul_entry_2_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (4 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall s0 s1 a x0 x1 y0 y1 : R,
  normalized_2 emin prec s0 s1 ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  normalized_2 emin prec x0 x1 ->
  normalized_2 emin prec y0 y1 ->
  0 <= a ->
  let '(t0, t1, b) := acc_mul_entry_2 emin prec tie_even s0 s1 a x0 x1 y0 y1 in
  fmt emin prec b /\
  normalized_2 emin prec t0 t1 /\
  Rabs ((t0 + t1) - ((s0 + s1) + ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1)))) <= (((3 * (1 + ((4 * u prec) * u prec))) / (1 - (4 * u prec))) + 4) * u prec ^ 2 * (Rabs (s0 + s1) + Rabs ((x0 + x1) * (y0 + y1))) + 2 * eta emin /\
  b = RN emin prec (a + ((Rabs x0) * (Rabs y0))).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `acc_mul_entry_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** acc_mul_2 on the guarded limbs of x and y (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation). **License:** algorithm: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/acc_mul_entry_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/acc_mul_entry_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`acc_mul_2`](acc_mul_2.md).

```
# acc.add_product(x, y) of Accumulator<T, 2> (milestone2.md, "The accumulator"): acc_mul_2 on the
# limbs of x and y guarded (rule R3, the factors of a fused operation: architecture.md). acc_mul_2
# only multiplies them, in mul_2_2 and in the sum of the magnitudes, which R3 alone does not guard;
# but a compiler that sees one of them to be 1 rewrites fma(x, 1, s) as x + s and fuses a product of
# the program into it (measured in acc_mul_1, the product of one limb, with Apple clang 21 under
# -ffp-contract=fast). After the guards each limb is a number of the format. Its claims are those
# of acc_mul_2: the guard is the identity on numbers of the format.

gx0          = guard(x0)
gx1          = guard(x1)
gy0          = guard(y0)
gy1          = guard(y1)
(t0, t1, b)  = acc_mul_2(s0, s1, a, gx0, gx1, gy0, gy1)
```

No stored brute-force run has judged this kernel yet.

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
- Anything about an operand that is not normalized, which only limbs given by the program can make: `from_limbs` in a build without checks, `from_limbs_unchecked`, or `limb[]` written directly.
